authors: Pires, M.C., Colosimo, E.A., Veloso, G.A. & Ferreira, R.S.B.
title: Interval-censored data with misclassification: a Bayesian approach
relevance: The exact statistical shape of our problem: an event known only to fall within an interval, detected by a test with imperfect SENSITIVITY and SPECIFICITY, with those accuracy parameters entering the likelihood as explicit corrections. That is our crown-loss product - loss located between two epochs, observed through a model whose recall is .51-.78 and whose precision we measure. Crucially it UNIFIES our two workstreams: the honest-measurement effort is not merely quality control, it produces the sensitivity and specificity that this estimator consumes. Without those numbers the change product cannot be de-biased; with them it can.

authors: Deng, Y., Zeng, D. & Wang, Y.
title: Semiparametric analysis of interval-censored data subject to inaccurate diagnoses with a terminal event
relevance: Current peer-reviewed treatment of interval censoring plus diagnostic inaccuracy, with a TERMINAL event - and crown removal is terminal in exactly that sense, since a felled tree does not return. Builds a Cox-type semiparametric model where sensitivity and specificity enter the data likelihood and NPMLE with an EM algorithm handles both censoring and misclassification together. This is the most statistically complete match the loop has found for the per-crown deliverable, and it accepts covariates - which is how height band, land-use context or radiometric cluster would enter as risk factors rather than as post-hoc stratifications.
